title: Portfolio Website Project Proposal
text:
Short Presentation Script
Hello everyone. My portfolio focuses on digital marketing and marketing analytics. My home page introduces my background and skills. The Digital Marketing Projects page includes website user experience, local SEO, and campaign planning. The Marketing Analytics Projects page includes GA4 website traffic analysis, R visualizations, a dashboard, and a Revealjs presentation. My main analytics goal is to understand which pages and traffic sources perform best and how to improve engagement. I plan to use GA4 data, descriptive statistics, and R charts. Right now, the sample charts are demonstrations, and I will replace them with actual data after tracking is verified. My resume is also available on the website. Thank you.

title: Marketing Data Visualization with R
text:
Project title: Exploring Marketing Performance Through R Visualization
Data and source: A documented course or approved marketing dataset; the chart below uses the explicitly synthetic CSV bundled with this portfolio.
Managerial problem: Raw performance tables are difficult for decision-makers to interpret quickly.
Target audience: Marketing analysts and marketing managers.
Research questions: How do metrics vary across acquisition channels? Which patterns deserve further investigation?
Expected business impact: Make performance differences easier to communicate and help prioritize follow-up analysis.
Quantitative methods: Grouped descriptive statistics, proportions, comparisons, and bar charts using R and ggplot2.

title: GA4 Portfolio Website Traffic Analysis
text:
Sample Analytics Workflow






Warning



Demo data only. The included CSV was created solely to demonstrate the R workflow. Do not present its values as actual traffic, and do not claim GA4 is installed until verified.



library(ggplot2)
d <- read.csv("data/ga4_sample.csv")
d$engagement_rate <- d$engaged_sessions / d$sessions
by_page <- aggregate(views ~ page, data=d, FUN=sum)
print(by_page)

                 page views
1   Digital Marketing    58
2                Home    83
3 Marketing Analytics    62
4              Resume    19

ggplot(by_page, aes(x=reorder(page, views), y=views)) +
  geom_col(fill="#806a83") + coord_flip() +
  labs(title="Example page views (synthetic data)", x="Page", y="Example views") +
  theme_minimal(base_size=12)









by_channel <- aggregate(cbind(sessions, engaged_sessions) ~ channel, data=d, FUN=sum)
by_channel$engagement_rate <- round(100 * by_channel$engaged_sessions / by_channel$sessions, 1)
print(by_channel)

         channel sessions engaged_sessions engagement_rate
1         Direct       59               43            72.9
2 Organic Search       81               62            76.5
3       Referral       32               23            71.9

title: GA4 Portfolio Website Traffic Analysis
section: How to Replace Sample Data with Actual GA4 Data
text:
How to Replace Sample Data with Actual GA4 Data

Create or verify a GA4 web data stream for the published portfolio website.
Add the measurement tag to the site, and verify collection with Realtime or DebugView.
Collect traffic over time and export GA4 reports containing comparable dimensions and metrics.
Convert the exported data to the columns date, channel, page, views, engaged_sessions, and sessions, or adapt the R code to match your export.
Replace data/ga4_sample.csv and remove the sample-data warning only after checking the real source and metric definitions.

title: GA4 Portfolio Website Traffic Analysis
text:
Limitations
The example dataset cannot establish visitor behavior or business impact. GA4 metrics must be interpreted with the appropriate date range, consent settings, and event definitions.
